name: Life Preservation: statistical-equivalence and equal-consideration invariant

anchor.source: US HHS Standard Values for Regulatory Analysis, 2024

invariants.statistical_equivalence: One expected death averted under risk-reduction aggregation receives VSL=13.1M at the chosen baseline
invariants.equal_consideration: No person assigned a lower baseline solely because of personal income, race, employment, disability, or wealth
invariants.boundary: Population risk reduction metric does not imply each individual has a legal cash claim of VSL
invariants.life_first: Compare safety intervention costs to monetized risk-reduction benefits, while retaining unmonetized human rights and distributional considerations

distinctions.individual_life: a human life; cannot be reduced to a monetary value by federal VSL
distinctions.restitution: requires identified injury, claim basis, causation and legal measure
distinctions.baseline_endowment: optional user policy hypothesis, not a balance owed by the government

federal_sources.name: HHS Standard Values for Regulatory Analysis 2024
EPA 2024 Guidelines for Preparing Economic Analyses Third Edition
OMB Circular A-4 mortality risk guidance

policy_notes: No compounding VSL back to 1931 as debt
No interpretation of VSL as damages award
No assertion that a person is literally worth only $13.1M
Do not double count deaths averted and separately valued life-years from same intervention
Benefit-cost analysis must assess the actual causal change in risk
